rationale: All three lenses (blind, edge-case, acceptance) ran and every spec/story criterion passes. One major regression was introduced: on a new-assistant publish, the per-document fallback swallows an embedding failure, so the service and router log 'Successfully indexed' where they previously logged an error (CR-001). There are 2 deferred findings, both accepted trade-offs from the approved spec: skips are logged but not recorded on IndexInfo, and transient errors such as ES outages or 429s take the per-document skip path. A total failure still marks the index FAILED through NoChunksImported, and the Azure embeddings client retries internally. 10 findings were dismissed: batch_size 0 is pre-existing config with the same pattern in the base processor; tiktoken offline download is a pre-existing o200k_base usage; a None description is ruled out because the field is typed str; the tokenizer approximation is a spec decision with 2x headroom; the trim-loop cost is bounded at 4000 tokens; there are a trailing U+FFFD, duplicate info logs, provider error text in logs, the zip strict flag on py3.12, and an unchanged metadata path.

findings.title: New-assistant publish failure swallowed and logged as success
findings.problem: index_single_entity(is_update=False), used for a new marketplace publish, now goes through the batch fallback. An embedding failure is caught and logged as a warning, and _add_documents returns normally.
findings.impact: PlatformIndexingService.index_single_assistant and the router _index_marketplace_assistant then log 'Successfully indexed assistant', although the assistant is missing from the index. Previously the exception reached the router's logger.error. This is a misleading observability regression for publish.
findings.recommendation: Keep fail-fast semantics for single-entity indexing regardless of is_update. For example, index_single_entity calls a direct store path, or _add_documents gets a fail_fast flag that index_single_entity sets, and moves progress only on success when not is_update. Add a test that a failing new-entity publish raises.
